c.tagline: A lakeside university town straddling the Swiss border on the shores of Lake Constance
langs: English (widely spoken in tourist and university areas)

card: Contactless and card payment are standard at hotels, restaurants, and shops; small market stalls and the harbor kiosks may prefer cash.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard; cross-border trips into Switzerland (Kreuzlingen) may carry a small surcharge

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number and typically reaches English-speaking dispatchers

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: The Altstadt is compact and highly walkable, with cobblestone lanes linking the cathedral, harbor, and Konzil building within a 15-20 minute stroll; Mainau Island and Reichenau require a short boat or bus ride.

safety.safety: Very safe; Konstanz is a low-crime university and lakeside town comfortable for solo travelers at any hour
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; standard caution applies around the train station and lakeside crowds in summer

hood_landmark.Hafen (Harbor District): Imperia statue and the Konzil building
hood_landmark.Petershausen: Rhine riverside promenade across the Old Rhine Bridge

hood_desc: The medieval core with the cathedral, Rathaus, and narrow shopping lanes — the natural base for most visitors and the liveliest part of town.
The lakefront harbor area where ferries depart for Mainau and Meersburg, anchored by the striking Imperia statue and the former Council building.
A residential district across the Rhine from the Altstadt, with a laid-back, local feel and riverside walking paths.
The university quarter south of the center, with a younger, more budget-friendly atmosphere and student-oriented cafes and bars.
The green, garden-island fringe of the city, home to Mainau's famous botanical gardens and quieter residential lakeshore.

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe to drink, sourced from Lake Constance.

transit.sys: Stadtwerke Konstanz (SWK) city bus network plus Lake Constance ferries (BSB)
transit.hours: Roughly 5am-midnight for buses; ferries run seasonal daytime schedules
transit.pay: Contactless card, bodo app, or cash on board; ferry tickets at the harbor kiosk
transit.map: Route maps at stadtwerke-konstanz.de and bsb.de
transit.note: The Altstadt is fully walkable; ferries are the scenic way to reach Mainau, Meersburg, and other lake towns

transport.air: Nearest airports are Friedrichshafen (FDH), about 30 km away, and Zurich (ZRH), about 1 hour away across the Swiss border
transport.train: Konstanz Hauptbahnhof has regional connections to Stuttgart, Zurich, and around Lake Constance; it's the southern terminus of German rail before the Swiss border
transport.bus: FlixBus and regional coaches connect Konstanz to Stuttgart, Freiburg, and Zurich
transport.ferry: Lake Constance ferries (BSB) connect Konstanz to Meersburg, Mainau, and other lakeside towns; a car ferry also crosses to Meersburg
transport.car: Reachable via the A81 autobahn or Swiss A7; the border with Kreuzlingen, Switzerland runs directly through the city, so a passport/ID is needed for crossing

airport.name: Friedrichshafen Airport
airport.transport: Regional train via Radolfzell; taxi transfer roughly €50-70

net.m: Excellent 4G/5G coverage throughout Konstanz and along Lake Constance
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels, cafes, and the university campus
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in cafes and public spaces in the Altstadt
net.ap: EU roaming covers most European visitors; a prepaid German SIM or eSIM is easy to buy at Friedrichshafen or Zurich Airport

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up or a small tip for good service is appreciated
tip.r: 5-10% is customary if service isn't already included — hand the tip directly to the server

landmarks: Konstanz Minster (Münster Unserer Lieben Frau)
This thousand-year-old cathedral hosted sessions of the Council of Constance; climbing its tower earns sweeping views over lake, Rhine and Alps.
Imperia Statue
Peter Lenk's rotating nine-metre courtesan, holding tiny emperor and pope in her palms, satirises the medieval Council from the harbour entrance.
Mainau Island
The famed Flower Island layers tulips, roses and dahlias around a baroque palace, butterfly house and ancient arboretum in Lake Constance.
Council Building (Konzilgebäude)
In this 1388 lakeside warehouse, the conclave of 1417 elected Pope Martin V, the only papal election ever held north of the Alps.
Niederburg Quarter
Konstanz's oldest quarter tangles medieval lanes, wine taverns and craft shops between the Minster and the Rhine's outflow.
Reichenau Island
A causeway reaches this UNESCO-listed monastic island, whose three Carolingian churches preserve some of Europe's oldest wall paintings.
Rheintorturm (Rhine Gate Tower)
A 14th-century defensive tower guards the point where the Rhine leaves Lake Constance, a favourite subject for evening photographers.
Rosgarten Museum
Inside a medieval guildhall, this charming museum displays the celebrated Chronicle of the Council and centuries of Lake Constance culture.
Hus House (Hus-Haus)
The reputed lodging of Czech reformer Jan Hus before his 1415 trial and execution now movingly documents his life and legacy.
Stadtgarten and Lake Promenade
Lakeside gardens with a bandstand and old plane trees offer front-row Alpine views, ferry watching and summer concerts by the harbour.

intl.to: Kreuzlingen & Weinfelden (Switzerland), with connections to Zurich & St Gallen
Schaffhausen & Basel (Switzerland) - via Singen on the High Rhine line

train.note: Konstanz station stands on the lakefront right beside the harbour and the old town, and the Swiss border station of Kreuzlingen is a ten-minute walk away - you can simply walk into Switzerland. German regional trains, the Seehas services run by SBB's German subsidiary, head west to Radolfzell, Singen and Engen for connections towards Stuttgart and the Black Forest, while Swiss Thurbo trains run along the lake shore and to Weinfelden for Zurich and St Gallen. There is no ICE to Konstanz itself, so the fastest German connections involve a change at Singen. German and Swiss fares are separate systems, so buy the Swiss leg from SBB rather than assuming a DB ticket covers it.

intl.to: Kreuzlingen (Switzerland) - cross-border city bus routes from Konstanz station

bus.note: Konstanz city buses run across the border into Kreuzlingen every few minutes from the stops in front of the railway station, so the frontier works more like a tram stop than a crossing - carry ID all the same. Long-distance coaches, principally FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/), use the same station forecourt on runs towards Stuttgart, Ulm and Munich; tickets are online only. For deeper Swiss destinations the train from Kreuzlingen is faster and more frequent than any coach.

intl.to: Meersburg (Germany) - car and passenger ferry from Konstanz-Staad, about 4 km north-east of the centre
Friedrichshafen (Germany) - catamaran from the harbour pier beside the railway station
Kreuzlingen, Stein am Rhein & Schaffhausen (Switzerland) - Untersee and Rhine boats from the harbour
Mainau, Meersburg & Friedrichshafen (Germany), with high-season sailings on to Lindau and Bregenz (Austria) - from the Konstanz harbour

ferry.note: Konstanz is a lake port, so boats here are ordinary transport rather than a sightseeing extra. The Meersburg car ferry sails from Staad, about 4 km north-east of the centre and reachable on city bus 1, running day and night all year and taking around 15 minutes; cars cannot be reserved and queues build on summer weekends. The passenger catamaran to Friedrichshafen leaves hourly from the pier next to the railway station and takes just under an hour, operating roughly from April to early October. BSB's White Fleet and the Swiss URh boats down the Rhine to Stein am Rhein and Schaffhausen are seasonal, broadly April to October, and cross the border, so carry a passport or ID card.

half.name: Lindau
half.blurb: A harbor town on the eastern shore of Lake Constance with a lighthouse, a stone lion statue at the pier, and a walkable old town.

half.name: Stein am Rhein
half.blurb: A small Swiss town where the Rhine leaves Lake Constance, known for medieval houses covered in painted frescoes along its main square.

half.name: Bregenz
half.blurb: An Austrian lakeside town with a cable car up Pfänder mountain and a floating summer stage used for the Bregenz Festival opera performances.

half.name: Schaffhausen (Rhine Falls)
half.blurb: A Swiss city near Europe's largest waterfall, the Rhine Falls, where boats and viewing platforms get close to the roaring drop.
